title: Unit econ: add cache hit-rate metrics + estimated cache savings attribution
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Motivation: Unit economics dashboard needs first-class cache visibility to explain $/1M output tokens movement and to quantify the impact of prefix/KV caching across models/regions/tiers. This PR adds cache hit-rate metrics (prefix + KV) into the unit economics aggregation + semantic layer and introduces an estimated cache savings attribution (USD + normalized per 1M output tokens). The intent is not to be perfect cost accounting, but to provide a stable, directional signal that Finance/Product can use in weekly reviews and to correlate with runtime/config changes. Summary of changes: (1) Extend metering aggregation to compute cache-eligible tokens, cache hit tokens, and hit rates for prefix and KV caches at the same grain as unit_econ_daily (day x model x region x tier). (2) Add estimated_cache_savings_usd and estimated_cache_savings_per_1m_output_tokens derived from avoided compute based on blended gpu_cost_per_output_token at the same grain (see docs for assumptions). (3) Update semantic layer views to expose new columns with stable names + add documentation comments for downstream consumers. (4) Add data quality checks to ensure hit rates are within [0,1] and savings estimates are non-negative; emit warnings when cache metrics are missing for a model/runtime that should support caching. Assumptions / caveats: Savings are estimated as cache_hit_output_token_equivalents * blended_gpu_cost_per_output_token for the slice. We intentionally exclude overhead allocation and network/storage costs from the savings estimate (those remain in blended cost). When cache telemetry is absent (older runtimes / partial ingestion), the new fields are NULL (not 0) to avoid implying a 0% cache rate. Backfill will populate once underlying cache telemetry is present; see ENG-2918 for broader historical backfill. Testing: Added unit tests around rate bounds + savings non-negativity; added a golden snapshot for a sample day partition; verified semantic layer query in staging console (filters: model/region/tier) renders without changing existing charts.
commits: analytics(unit-econ): aggregate prefix/kv cache tokens + hit rates
analytics(unit-econ): compute estimated cache savings (usd, per-1m output tokens)
semantic-layer: expose cache metrics on unit_econ_daily_v1
docs: document cache columns + estimation methodology
tests: add bounds checks and snapshot for cache metrics
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we be explicit about the grain for cache tokens? Are these computed from request-level telemetry or runtime counters? Also please confirm NULL vs 0 behavior for missing cache metrics.

Caleb Johnson (author): Grain matches unit_econ_daily (day x model x region x tier). Tokens are derived from metering events where runtime emits cache counters (prefix_cache_{eligible,hit}_tokens and kv_cache_{eligible,hit}_tokens). If a slice has no cache counters (e.g., older runtime), fields stay NULL. Added note in semantic-layer docs + a check that we never coerce to 0 downstream.

Nadia Rahman (review): Savings estimate uses blended_gpu_cost_per_output_token for the same slice; that can include mix of requests with/without cache telemetry, which may under/over estimate. Can we scope savings to only cache-eligible traffic?

Caleb Johnson (author): Agree. Updated calculation to use gpu_cost_usd / output_tokens only for rows where cache_eligible_tokens > 0 (per-request level before aggregation). If eligible tokens are 0, savings remains NULL. Added unit tests for this path.

Thomas Baird (review): Concern about cardinality / performance: adding more columns is fine, but are we adding joins to compute these? unit_econ_daily_aggregate.sql already heavy. Please ensure query plan doesn’t add high-cardinality intermediate steps.

Caleb Johnson (author): No new joins; all cache counters come from the same metering_events_daily rollup we already scan for tokens/latency. I kept everything within the same aggregation pass and added only SUM()s + SAFE_DIVIDE hit rates. Included an EXPLAIN in the PR notes; stage runtime was +3.1% scan time for the job, no increase in output partitions.

Allison Grant (review): Please add data-quality guardrails + an alert hook if we get negative savings or hit rates > 1. Also define expected nullability so dashboards don’t page for missing cache data on older models.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added bounds checks (0..1) and non-negative savings check with WARN-only when cache fields are NULL. The alerting wiring itself is in observability-pack PR; here we just emit the check results to the existing unit-econ data quality stream.
Logan Wright (review): Docs: can we call out that savings excludes overhead and discounts and is intended for attribution/explain panel only?
Caleb Johnson (author): Updated docs/internal/unit-econ/metric_dictionary.md + semantic-layer markdown to call this out explicitly and added a disclaimer snippet for the explain panel consumers.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Thanks for tightening the eligible-traffic calculation and the NULL semantics.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved with the updated methodology + tests.
Thomas Baird (approval): Approved; performance notes look good.
release_notes: Internal-only: unit economics datasets now include prefix/KV cache hit rates and an estimated cache savings attribution (USD + per 1M output tokens).
